fields.title: 📖 Makān and Nuzūl among the early Imāms
fields.body:
🖋️ **Ḥammād b. Zayd** was asked about the ḥadīth of the **Nuzūl**, whether it means that Allah moves from place to place. He said:

***“He is in His place; He draws near to His creation as He wills.”***

🖋️ **Isḥāq b. Rāhawayh** rejected the objection of whether the ʿArsh becomes empty at the Nuzūl, and explained in substance that Allah is able to descend without the ʿArsh becoming empty.

🖋️ **al-Fuḍayl b. ʿIyāḍ** said:

***“If the Jahmī says: I deny a Lord who departs from His place, then say: I believe in a Lord who does what He wills.”***

👉🏼 **Explanation:** These early statements affirm the transmitted **Nuzūl** (descent) and at the same time reject a creaturely notion of changing place, movement, or corporeality. The way is: affirm what has come, and leave the how to Allah.

🌙 **Conclusion:** The Salaf affirmed the ḥadīth of the Nuzūl without **Tashbīh** and without **Taʿṭīl**. The false frame of thought of the Jahmiyyah is rejected, not the revelation.

immutable.source: 📝 Ibn Taymiyyah, Sharḥ Ḥadīth an-Nuzūl, S. 40–41; über al-Khallāl, Ibn Baṭṭah und weitere Überlieferungswege.
immutable.scholar: Ḥammād b. Zayd, Isḥāq b. Rāhawayh, al-Fuḍayl b. ʿIyāḍ
